svg.text: The chain from broken input to recommendation
Each link is forced by the one above it. Every figure was recomputed from the source CSVs.
The sales file is truncated, so sales cannot measure the year
SalesFINAL12312016.csv holds exactly 1,048,575 data rows — the Excel worksheet ceiling — and stops on 24 February 2016.
January is complete (31 of 31 days, 79 of 79 stores). February holds 11 stores of 79. March to December are absent entirely.
rows · 2 months · 1 usable
So movement is derived from the inventory identity instead
opening 4,219,275 + received 33,584,377 − closing 4,885,776 = 32,917,876 units depleted, computed at SKU-store grain.
This never touches the truncated file. It is depletion, not sales — it absorbs shrinkage and adjustments — and that is stated on the measure.
units · complete, all 12 months
The headline that produces is healthy
COGS $310,344,546 ÷ average inventory $73,926,741 = 4.20x turnover. Days of supply 54.2. Sell-through 87.1%.
On these three numbers alone the business turns its stock roughly every eight weeks and moves 87% of everything available to it.
the number a dashboard usually stops at
But the average conceals the tail — and the tail is where the money is
Ranked at SKU-store grain, days of supply runs: median 59 · p90 431 · p99 3,285 · max 43,435. 2,508 SKU-stores hold over ten years of cover.
$26,764,857 (33.6%) sits past 180 days. A further $3,458,493 (4.3%) showed zero depletion across the whole of 2016.
37.9% of closing stock is not turning
And it is concentrated, which makes it actionable
Five stores of 80 hold 40.7% of all dead stock. Wine is 42.6% of closing stock value but 65.9% of the stock that never moved.
62,665 SKU-stores are overstocked and 5,788 are dead — out of 276,389. This is a short list, not a portfolio-wide problem.
$2.28M wine · $1.18M spirits
dead stock, by product class
RECOMMENDATION
Manage the tail, not the headline. $30.2M — 37.9% of closing stock — is not turning, and the 4.20x average hides it.
Start with wine: it is 43% of the money on the shelf and 66% of the money that never moved, so it is the highest-yield place to cut buying.
Clearing 20% of the 365+ day band alone releases $2.9M of working capital, against a total 2016 purchase spend of $321.9M.
Caveat carried forward: margin figures are January 2016 only and use a Dec-2017 list price. Turnover, days of supply, dead stock and overstock are full-year and complete.
